source.title: MASCing: Configurable Mixture-of-Experts Behavior via Activation Steering Masks
source.authors: Jona Te Lintelo; Li-Chao Wu; Marina Krček; Sengim Karayalçin; S. Picek

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites and briefly describes work on a residual-stream refusal direction, but its experiments intervene on MoE routing logits with learned steering masks. They do not test the cited direction or any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal-related behavior under its own routing-mask intervention. Those results are recorded as findings about a related mechanism, not as tests of the residual-stream direction. The MMLU/GSM8K utility results concern the paper's routing masks, not removal or addition of the claimed direction, so they are not included as claim-version rows.
record.test_reason: The study cites Arditi et al. only in background and related work. Its experiments learn sparse masks on MoE routing logits using an LSTM surrogate. It never computes, ablates or adds a difference-in-means residual-stream direction, makes no weight edit, and does not test multi-direction, harm-vs-refusal, transfer, training or reasoning-model accounts. Its refusal-related results concern a different mechanism (expert routing), so they bear on no version. Some might read the jailbreak-defense results as relevant to V3, but no attack is shown to act by suppressing the direction, and there is no training against its ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that sparse routing-logit masks found via an LSTM surrogate can strengthen or relax safety behavior in seven MoE models without retraining. They also report a modest utility cost (average 4.1% decline on MMLU/GSM8K), which they describe as preserving general capabilities. They draw no conclusion about the residual-stream refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an LSTM surrogate to identify expert-routing interventions and applies masks to routing logits; it does not compute or intervene on a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction.
record.method_sensitivity: For the paper's routing-mask method, outcomes vary with steering strength α, sparsity threshold τ, and regularization λ; the authors report that excessive α or τ=0 can degrade performance, while τ=0.1 gives the highest defense success in their tested sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse learned masks on MoE routing logits raised multi-turn jailbreak defense success from 52.5% to 83.9% on average across seven MoE models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal/safety behavior in MoE models can be strengthened by steering expert-routing logits, without weight changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Routing-logit masks raised adult-content compliance from 52.6% to 82.0% in four models that refused such requests. Average MMLU/GSM8K utility fell by 4.1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Category-specific refusal in MoE models can be suppressed by steering expert routing, at a modest utility cost.

record.problems: The experiments use routing-logit masks rather than the claimed residual-stream direction, so they do not establish whether the direction mediates refusal. The reported success rates have no uncertainty estimates stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Utility benchmark results in Table 4 were not extracted because they evaluate the paper's routing masks, not an intervention on the claimed direction.

untested.parts: All of it: no difference-in-means residual direction, no ablation or addition, no harmless-prompt induction.
All of it: no weight edit or abliteration.
All of it: no analysis of jailbreaks suppressing the direction, no adversarial training against ablation.

record.verdict_notes: Table 5 (vs SteerMoE) and Table 6 (vs expert steering) compare the study's own method with others; they are rightly not rows. The utility results in Table 4 concern routing masks, not the direction, so leaving them out is fine for this phenomenon. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The difference-in-means residual direction, its ablation or addition, and the claimed harmful-request refusal and harmless-request induction effects.
No weight edit or abliteration is evaluated.
No attack is tested for suppressing the residual direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
No affine, cone, or multiple-residual-direction account of refusal is tested.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No transfer of the residual direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
The study does not vary refusal training or its timing.
No test of the claimed direction in reasoning models is reported.

relation.reason: The refusal direction is mentioned in one background sentence and one related-work sentence. It is neither used nor tested.

tranche.reason: Arditi et al. is cited only in background (Sec. 2.2) and related work (Sec. 8). The method masks MoE routing logits using an LSTM surrogate. It never computes, ablates or adds a residual-stream refusal direction, and no result bears on any version.

source_check.notes: All Table 2/3 success rates are the best of a hyperparameter grid (Sec. 6.1/6.2), seemingly tuned on the evaluation set, and none bears on a refusal_direction version. The authors_conclusion says safety was relaxed in seven models, but the adult-content result covers only four: three models did not refuse such requests.
